description:
IEU UNIVERSITY (PUEBLA, MEXICO) We are a multidisciplinary team of 18- and 19-year-old undergraduate students from IEU University in Puebla, Mexico.
As young Latin American researchers passionate about applied artificial intelligence, and Earth sciences, we built AETHERIS-7 from scratch without institutional supercomputing infrastructure Our goal was to prove that open environmental data—combined with rigorous numerical calculus and low-cost cloud computing—can empower civil protection
summary:
We developed AETHERIS-7, a low-cost, advanced artificial intelligence hybrid numerical-neural system built from scratch using a 7-subnet architecture to generate hyperlocal weather forecasts and issue early alerts for extreme climate events without relying on supercomputers.

Our project addresses the challenge by fusing classical numerical calculus with a custom 7-subnet deep learning cascade (integrating Conv1D, LSTM, TCN, and temporal attention). Trained on 418,733 historical NOAA NCEI reports (1998–2025) and powered by live Open-Meteo inference, AETHERIS-7 transforms standard meteorological data into high-resolution (15-minute) probabilistic forecasts with P10–P90 quantile uncertainty bands and severe anomaly alerts.

This is critically important because traditional numerical weather prediction requires massive computational infrastructure, leaving vulnerable communities without timely, localized early warnings. Trained in approximately one hour on Google Colab by 18- and 19-year-old undergraduate students at IEU University in Puebla, Mexico, AETHERIS-7 proves that high-precision, leak-free climate intelligence can be democratized and deployed anywhere at near-zero cost.
details:
AETHERIS-7 is an end-to-end operational forecasting pipeline that ingests historical and real-time meteorological observations to predict hyperlocal weather states and extreme anomalies. The workflow operates in two main stages:

  1. Numerical Calculus Feature Engineering: Using 418,733 historical observations from NOAA NCEI (Station USW00013743, 1998–2025) alongside live Open-Meteo API streams, the pipeline quadruples temporal resolution down to 15-minute intervals via PCHIP (Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial) interpolation. To capture physical atmospheric dynamics without future data leakage, it extracts change rates using causal Savitzky-Golay derivatives and computes cumulative energy and moisture balances via Simpson's 1/3 numerical integration.
  2. 7-Subnet Deep Learning Cascade: The engineered physical features feed into a specialized cascade of seven neural subnetworks combining 1D Convolutions (Conv1D), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), and Temporal Attention mechanisms. Instead of outputting rigid single-point deterministic guesses, the cascade predicts calibrated P10–P90 quantile uncertainty bands and flags severe weather anomalies.
  • Democratization of Early Warnings: Eliminates the need for multi-million-dollar HPC (High-Performance Computing) clusters, enabling local municipalities, agricultural sectors, and civil protection agencies in developing regions to run hyperlocal forecasting.
  • Actionable Risk Management: By providing P10–P90 uncertainty bands rather than isolated numbers, decision-makers can evaluate worst-case scenarios (P90) with quantifiable confidence.
  • Rapid Replicability: Because the entire architecture trains in ~1 hour on accessible cloud GPUs and infers via public APIs, it can be rapidly recalibrated for any weather station worldwide.
  • Data Sources: NOAA NCEI historical archives (Station USW00013743) and Open-Meteo API for live operational inference.
  • Programming & Libraries: Python ecosystem for scientific computing and deep learning (implementing PCHIP, Savitzky-Golay filters, Simpson's 1/3 integration, and neural architectures via TensorFlow/Keras/PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas).
  • Hardware & Cloud Infrastructure: Google Colaboratory (Colab) cloud environment, completing full 7-subnet training in approximately 1 hour without dedicated local server hardware.

Rather than throwing raw data into a massive "black-box" foundation model, AETHERIS-7 embeds mathematical physics directly into the data representation. Using PCHIP preserves monotonicity and prevents artificial overshoots (Runge's phenomenon) during 15-minute upsampling; causal Savitzky-Golay derivatives give the neural networks explicit atmospheric velocity and acceleration signals; and Simpson's 1/3 integration tracks thermodynamic and moisture accumulation over time. This mathematical pre-digestion allows a lightweight 7-subnet cascade to achieve high precision in just one hour of training.

Factors Considered by the Team (Unbiased Validation & Rigor) developed by 18- and 19-year-old undergraduate students at IEU University (Puebla, Mexico), our primary technical priority was eliminating data leakage and evaluation bias—a common flaw in time-series AI:

  • Causal Filtering: All derivatives and interpolations are strictly causal during inference so future information never contaminates past states.
  • Chronological Safety Gap: We partitioned the dataset using a strict chronological 70/10/10/10 split enforced with a 48-hour safety gap between partitions to prevent synoptic autocorrelation bleed.
  • Raw-Data Evaluation: Model metrics are evaluated strictly against raw, uninterpolated ground-truth observations, ensuring our accuracy reflects real-world sensor measurements rather than synthetic interpolated points.
